headline: Digital marketing for schools in Delhi: plan around the DoE admission calendar
card_title: Digital marketing for schools in Delhi
card_text: How Delhi schools can plan Google, Meta and review campaigns around the DoE nursery schedule, points criteria and parent trust.
intro:
Digital marketing for schools in Delhi works differently from almost anywhere else in India. For nursery, KG and Class 1, private unaided schools follow a timetable and a points system set by the Directorate of Education (DoE). Parents can apply to many schools for a ₹25 registration fee, and the schools you compete with all open and close on the same dates. That changes what your ads should say, who they should reach and when you should spend.

Most guides on this topic are generic lists of tips. This one is built around the Delhi admission cycle: what to do before criteria go up, during the application window, after the lists come out, and through the rest of the year when parents are quietly judging your school online.

sections.h2: How Delhi entry-level admissions shape your marketing
sections.html:
In the 2026-27 cycle, about 1,741 private unaided schools in Delhi ran nursery admissions on one DoE schedule. Schools had to upload their admission criteria and points by late November 2025, parents applied from 4 to 27 December, and the first selection list came out in late January 2026. A few rules from that cycle matter for marketing:

  • Points decide open seats. Each school publishes its own criteria, and neighbourhood distance usually carries the most weight. Sibling and alumni points are also common.
  • Applying is cheap. The registration fee is ₹25 and buying the prospectus is optional, so parents apply widely. Your job is to be one of the schools they want, not just one they applied to.
  • 25% of entry-level seats are for EWS, DG and CWSN children and are filled through the DoE's central online lottery, not by the school.
  • Age rules changed. From 2026-27, nursery (Balvatika 1) is for children aged 3+ to 4 as on 31 March, with KG and Class 1 following in sequence.

The DoE issues a fresh notice every year. At the time of writing the 2027-28 schedule had not been published, so check edudel.nic.in before you fix your ad dates.

sections.h2: Target the neighbourhood your points reward
sections.html:
This is the most common waste we see in school ads in Delhi. A school gives most of its points to children living within a few kilometres, then runs Meta ads across all of South or West Delhi. Parents outside the radius apply, score low, and never get a seat. You paid for an enquiry that could never become an admission.

Start from your own criteria sheet:

  1. Map the distance bands that earn the most points and set your ad locations to match them, using pin-drop radius targeting rather than whole districts.
  2. Add the colonies and sectors inside that radius to your ad copy and landing page, for example "for families in Dwarka Sectors 6 to 12" or "near Janakpuri".
  3. Put a simple distance checker or a clear map on your admissions page so parents can see whether they qualify before they fill the form.
  4. Run a smaller, separate campaign for higher classes and Class 11, where seats depend on vacancies and your own admission process, so a wider radius can make sense.

sections.h2: Build parent trust before the window opens
sections.html:
Parents in Delhi shortlist schools months before December. They read Google reviews, ask in society WhatsApp groups and look at your website on their phone. When the application window opens, the shortlist is mostly made. That means October and November work matters more than December ads.

  • Google Business Profile. Real photos of classrooms, play areas and transport, admission dates in posts, and a reply to every review. Our Google Business Profile checklist for Delhi covers the full setup.
  • An honest admissions page. Your criteria and points, fee structure, transport routes and a short campus video. Hiding fees until the visit is the fastest way to lose a parent.
  • Teacher and campus content. Short videos of a nursery class in progress, the safety measures at the gate, the meals served. Parents of three-year-olds care about care, not toppers.
  • Reviews from current parents. Ask after a good parent-teacher meeting or annual day, not in a mass message. Never write reviews yourself or offer anything in exchange for them.

sections.h2: Google and Meta campaigns for Delhi school admissions
sections.html:
Google Search catches parents who are already looking; Meta reaches parents who will be looking soon. Most schools need both, with budgets that change through the season.

ChannelWhat to runWhat to measure
Google SearchKeywords such as "nursery admission in Rohini", "CBSE school near me" and your school name, limited to your radiusCalls, admissions page visits, campus tour bookings
Google MapsA complete profile with reviews, photos and admission postsDirection requests and calls from the profile
Meta (Facebook and Instagram)Campus tour and open house ads with real video, aimed at parents in your points radiusTour bookings and attendance, not just form fills
WhatsAppClick-to-WhatsApp ads and an instant reply with dates, criteria and a tour linkReply time and tours booked from chats
RemarketingReminders to parents who visited the admissions page as the form deadline nearsApplications completed

The offer should be a campus visit or open house, not "apply now". Parents can apply anywhere for ₹25; a visit is what moves you to the top of their list. Our Google Ads team and Meta ads team set these up with call and form tracking from day one.

sections.h2: A season calendar for Delhi schools
sections.html:
Treat this as a pattern based on recent DoE cycles. Confirm the official dates for your year before booking budgets.

WhenWhat parents are doingWhat to run
August to OctoberResearching schools, attending open days, asking other parentsGoogle profile clean-up, review requests, campus videos, early open house ads
Late NovemberReading each school's criteria and pointsPublish your criteria clearly, start Search ads, open house reminders
DecemberFilling in applications across several schoolsHighest budget: Search, Meta tour ads, WhatsApp replies, remarketing to unfinished applications
January to MarchChecking lists, waiting lists and pointsClear updates on your site and WhatsApp, fast replies to queries, warm welcome for selected families
April to JulyClass 11 stream choices after Class 10 results; families moving into the areaClass 11 and mid-session campaigns with a wider radius

sections.h2: Follow up in minutes and track cost per admission
sections.html:
A parent who sends an enquiry at 9 pm is often comparing three schools that evening. If your office replies the next afternoon, another school has already booked the tour. Set up an instant WhatsApp reply with the dates, criteria link and a tour booking option, then have the admissions team call within the same working day. Our guide to WhatsApp marketing for business explains the setup.

Then track every enquiry through four steps: enquiry, tour booked, tour attended, admission. Cost per lead on its own misleads schools. A cheap lead from outside your points radius costs more than an expensive one from the next block who joins. Report cost per tour attended and cost per admission by channel, and move budget each week towards whatever fills seats.

• Starting ads in December. By then most parents already have a shortlist.
  • Advertising beyond the points radius for entry-level classes, which fills the inbox with families who cannot get a seat.
  • Implying EWS or DG seats can be secured through the school. Those seats go through the DoE lottery; say so clearly and point parents to the official portal.
  • Making the prospectus compulsory to get basic information. It is optional for parents, and hiding criteria or fees behind it loses trust.
  • Using children's photos without written parent consent. Get consent in writing and keep a record.
  • Promising outcomes. Show your teaching, facilities and care; let parents draw their own conclusions.

faqs: When should a Delhi school start marketing for nursery admissions?

Start in August or September. Parents research and shortlist in the autumn, so reviews, campus videos and open house ads need to be running well before the DoE application window, which in recent cycles opened in late November or early December.
How can a school in Delhi get more nursery admission enquiries?

Target parents inside the distance bands your criteria reward, publish your criteria, fees and transport clearly, keep your Google Business Profile active with reviews, and promote campus tours on Google and Meta with fast WhatsApp follow-up.
Can schools advertise EWS seats in Delhi?

Schools can explain that EWS, DG and CWSN seats exist, but these seats are allotted through the DoE's central online lottery, not by the school. Ads should point parents to the official process rather than suggest the school can secure a seat.
How much should a Delhi school spend on admission ads?

It depends on your seats, radius and competition. A sensible approach is a modest budget from August to build trust, the largest share in December during the application window, and a smaller budget for Class 11 and mid-session admissions. Judge it by cost per admission, not cost per lead.
